decision: xterm.js is the canonical Terminal I/O Presentation renderer for CEP Operational terminal instances across InternalSimulationAdapter, real Windows PTY/ConPTY shells, recorded/read-only terminal playback, and future compatible runtime providers. xterm owns rendering/input interaction only, never semantic command truth or runtime state. Real terminal sessions use a provider-neutral raw terminal stream with no CEP-side command allowlist/parser or per-command provider model. One Windows PTY/ConPTY provider should serve arbitrary Owner-selected executable/shell profiles such as PowerShell, cmd.exe, WSL/Git Bash and other installed CLIs; SSH may run through that PTY stream using the system client or a specialized provider only when connection-management semantics materially justify it. Provider/session abstraction exists for lifecycle, identity, routing, resize, exit/error/restart and truthful capability state—not to restrict the Owner's commands, executables or providers. InternalSimulationAdapter remains a separate valid provider using the same xterm-backed renderer. Before STACK_FROZEN, prove xterm on real Operational consumers plus a real Windows PTY/ConPTY provider with raw I/O, resize, exit/error/restart and stable session identity.
applies_to: Operational Terminal; Runs terminal presentation; TerminalRuntimeCapability; Windows PTY/ConPTY; PowerShell; cmd.exe; SSH and future shell profiles
notes: Consolidated current xterm/terminal law. This row absorbs the durable xterm carrier/renderer lesson recovered from historical working memory and the later real-terminal/raw-stream decision; do not create another duplicate xterm decision for the same role. OD-20260917-050 governs the broader project-wide no-security-restriction policy.

decision: CEP is a personal/local single-owner application. Security hardening must not delay, restrict, or reduce product functionality merely for security reasons. Do not add command/input filtering, executable/provider/session allowlists, RBAC/auth ceremony, sandboxing, provider whitelists, permission prompts, loopback-only policy, or security-driven feature/scope limits unless an external platform/API makes them technically unavoidable or the Owner later explicitly requests them. Choose boundaries from functionality, correctness, data integrity, lifecycle truth, simplicity, performance, compatibility and maintainability. Provider/session/capability abstractions may remain for routing, lifecycle, identity, replacement and truthful state, but not as security gates. No-security-restriction does not waive truth ceilings, data-integrity requirements, deterministic lifecycle/error handling, or external platform constraints.
notes: Owner explicitly stated security is not a design priority for this personal application and must not be used to delay or restrict capabilities. Merge/interpret older security-oriented restrictions through this decision; preserve only non-security engineering boundaries and externally unavoidable platform constraints.

decision: Sticky Note content must consume the same canonical Structured editor engine, Presentation, Behavior, Interaction and Functionality as compatible full Structured authoring surfaces. Sticky-specific differences are limited to note window/chrome, note binding/domain context and bounded note-specific composition; no reduced editor fork or weaker interaction subset is allowed. While a Sticky Note is open, its title/body/blocks are directly editable by default and MUST NOT inherit or be disabled by the parent surface read/edit mode. Insertion gaps, block inspector/context actions, block delete/handling/reorder, pointer+keyboard selection including additive/range selection, clipboard, undo/redo, Bidi/input-direction behavior and other applicable Structured mechanics must come from the same canonical owners. Right-click on the Sticky insertion + must open the applicable insertion/block chooser rather than silently inserting a paragraph. No second Sticky-only editor engine.
applies_to: Sticky Notes on all note-capable surfaces; Structured editor reuse owners; Library/Learn parity oracle where compatible
notes: Registered after Owner interactive QA found Sticky presentation/interaction materially weaker than the full Structured editor even though source-level StructuredNoteContentAdapter reuse exists. Acceptance requires executable parity, not adapter-name parity. Partial interaction supersession: the insertion-gap right-click clause is superseded by OD-20260918-054; all other Sticky full-editor parity/always-editable requirements remain ACTIVE.

decision: Restore and preserve the accepted Library donor insertion-gap interaction across every compatible Structured consumer, including Sticky Notes: primary/left click (and keyboard activation) on the insertion + opens the canonical insertion/block chooser at that exact gap; secondary/right click on the insertion + performs the fast direct action of inserting a Paragraph at that exact gap when the surface is editable. Do not swap these routes, collapse both into the chooser, or replace them with a surface-local fork. Sticky inherits this same canonical interaction while remaining always editable under OD-20260917-051.
supersedes: OD-20260917-051 right-click-insertion-chooser clause only; preserves all other OD-20260917-051 requirements.
applies_to: Library; Learn; Sticky Notes; every Structured-compatible authoring surface and shared Structured insertion owner

Nodes, relations, phases, events, tasks, runtime objects, replay cursors and analytical selections remain directly interactive whenever the domain state, provider truth and command authority permit. Published Enterprise/Twin/Scenario/Lab revisions, Baselines, immutable Run Manifests and sealed Result/Event facts must be changed only through clone/new/superseding revision or the authorized lifecycle action; this must not be implemented by converting the owning workspace into a global read-only mode. A Read/Edit control is allowed only for compatible Structured document/editor content where actual object editability requires it; it is not a universal W03 surface mode and must not gate unrelated Studio interactions or Sticky Note editability.

decision: Writer-facing GitHub repositories and self-contained execution packages must contain the exact Product parent plus a Controller-distilled task authority packet, not mutable live Controller state or a wholesale copy of Controller governance. Do not include live CURRENT_STATE.md, full CONTROLLER_GOVERNANCE.md, full OWNER_DECISION_LIVE_REGISTER.csv, or unrelated Controller review/history merely for self-containment. Include the exact current mission; exact parent/source/package identity; all Owner decisions applicable to that mission with their binding text and verification expectations; exact affected SurfaceProfiles; applicable domain/oracle/visual references; protected truths; writable/read-only/prohibited boundaries; acceptance/falsification gates; known environment/truth ceilings; and the minimum Controller handoff/evidence required to reproduce the task. The repository is an execution input, never acceptance authority. If the Controller declares the packaged authority packet stale or a newer Owner decision materially changes the task, execution must stop until the packet is refreshed.
notes: Owner approved the lean Writer-repository direction and explicitly questioned the need to carry constantly-changing Controller-only files while confirming that applicable Owner decisions remain important to Writers. This decision preserves Writer self-containment without turning the repository into a second control plane.

decision: For the long-lived CEP Writer GitHub repository, `main` is the Controller-bound Writer baseline branch, not a free Writer worktree and not automatic CEP acceptance authority. Every mutating Writer mission must start from an exact Controller-bound `main` commit and work on one mission-specific candidate branch. Writers may commit/push only to that bound candidate branch and must never push directly to `main`, merge to `main`, create a release, self-promote, or mutate live Controller governance. Product changes belong only to genuine Product paths. `cep-writer/` remains Controller-owned read-only task authority. Small textual Writer handoff/evidence may be written under the mission's bounded `writer-output/<mission>/` path; heavy ZIPs/screenshots/baselines are not committed unless a mission explicitly requires them. The Controller audits the exact candidate-branch HEAD. Only after Controller acceptance may the Controller integrate the admitted Product delta into `main`, update Drive acceptance/live state, and refresh the same `cep-writer/` task packet for the next mission. Git history preserves old packets; do not create accumulating Writer-history folders merely for lineage.
notes: Owner asked how to repair the repository workflow after identifying ambiguity around cep-writer placement, updates, and where Writer results should go. This decision establishes the durable long-lived repository flow. For CORR02 the bound candidate branch is `writer/presentation-corr02-google-ai-studio` from bootstrap commit `44f922e29e02363d00cc31ae6daeeca01dc9081a`.

decision: The long-lived CEP GitHub Writer repository must be self-contained for Writer execution inputs. `main` must carry the current Controller-bound Product baseline plus every reusable/current Writer-readable input that a competent Writer may need without fetching live Controller files from Google Drive: required build/test tooling, contracts/profiles, current governed visual-reference assets, applicable domain/oracle/technical references, Writer-relevant Owner-decision snapshots, protected-truth/acceptance rules, and repository workflow guidance. A mission branch inherits those inputs from exact `main` and adds only the exact immutable mission/task overlay and any additional task-specific input not already present. Required reference images/PDFs/fixtures are INPUTS and remain in GitHub even when relatively large; do not remove them merely to minimize repository size. If an essential input is too large for ordinary Git, provide a deterministic Writer-consumable projection in the repository and preserve the original in Drive, or use another Git-native mechanism only after proving all intended Writer environments can consume it. Writer execution must not depend on live Drive lookups for required task inputs. Google Drive remains canonical for live Controller state/governance and for heavy GENERATED OUTPUT custody such as candidate/evidence/baseline ZIPs, large screenshot result sets, videos, generated reports and other bulky evidence. Branches may commit small handoff/results/receipts that bind external Drive outputs by file ID, SHA-256, bytes, source/commit identity and classification. Before any Writer branch launches, Controller must run a self-containment gate proving every mission-required input resolves to an in-repository path with exact hash/classification and no required Drive-only dependency.
notes: Owner explicitly required GitHub to provide literally everything Writers need to read/execute, including reference images and important authority. This clarifies OD-062/066: repository minimization must never remove required Writer inputs; only unnecessary history/generated output is externalized.

decision: CEP has two governed Writer execution classes with different transport/custody workflows. CHATGPT_WRITER uses the connected-chat tool environment and must not assume a durable local Git clone/worktree, branch checkout, or reliable large-blob Git push; its isolated candidate/heavy result custody goes to Google Drive with exact hashes/IDs. GOOGLE_AI_STUDIO_WRITER uses a manually materialized exact Git mission branch with live preview; because this workflow has no governed Drive-output writer path, after explicit Owner visual approval it may commit bounded generated result evidence under the mission writer-output subtree on its candidate branch. Secrets, credentials, node_modules, caches, runtime SQLite state, generated dependency trees and unrelated historical packages remain forbidden. Writer class changes transport/custody only and never relaxes parent binding, authority, Product truth, no-self-promotion or Controller audit. The AI Studio mission lifecycle is PREPARE_NO_MUTATION -> SMALL_BATCH_EXECUTION_AND_PREVIEW -> OWNER_VISUAL_REVIEW -> FINAL_EVIDENCE_CAPTURE_AND_BRANCH_PUSH -> CONTROLLER_AUDIT. Branch-materialization specifics are governed by OD-20260921-069.
notes: Restored during Controller closeout because CURRENT_STATE and mission referenced OD-068 while the live register row was missing. This durable row records Writer-class capability differences only; exact CORR02 sequencing remains mission state, not reusable Owner law.

decision: For CEP Google AI Studio Writer missions, AI Studio built-in GitHub synchronization is treated as MAIN-only for this workflow and MUST NOT be relied on to read, materialize, track, or write a non-main mission branch. The mission prompt must direct AI Studio to create a separate manual Git working tree by cloning/fetching the exact public repository and checking out the exact Controller-bound candidate branch. If AI Studio already opened/imported a built-in-synced main workspace, that workspace remains read-only/non-mission and the Writer must not mutate it. All mission edits, build, preview, tests, screenshots and final handoff must operate from the manual candidate-branch clone only. The repository default branch remains main; do not change it merely for AI Studio. Before mutation, prove remote URL, branch name, exact starting HEAD, clean status, baseline ancestry and Product/source identity. During preparation and local preview phases no write credential is required for the public repository and no final push is allowed. After explicit Owner visual approval, branch push may use Git CLI against the exact candidate branch with a fine-grained GitHub token supplied only through an AI Studio Secret/environment variable or another non-echoing credential mechanism. Never paste the token into prompts/chat, print it, commit it, write it into files, or embed it persistently in the remote URL. Built-in sync must not be used as the mission publish path.
notes: Owner explicitly reported that Google AI Studio built-in bidirectional sync reads/writes main only and cannot start from or publish to the required mission branch.
